title: 164. Dating and mental health in our 20s

sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, Guaranteed Human.
sentences.zh: 这是一个iHeart播客，保证真人录制。

sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在以一种切实可行的方式将健康放在首位，而让我保持动力的法宝就是我的WHOOP手环。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love WHOOP, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我特别看重数据，这就是为什么我喜欢WHOOP，因为它能让我真切地看到为什么我的身体在不同日子里会有不同的感觉，为什么我的跑步状态会有所不同，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我有时注意力不太集中。

sentences.en: WHOOP effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: WHOOP能轻松追踪我的睡眠、运动强度、恢复情况、压力水平，最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供所有的这些数据和规律，以便我能做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该放松，什么时候该拼搏。

sentences.en: New members can try WHOOP with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在正式订阅前，可以免费试用WHOOP 30天。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com 并在斜杠后输入 psychology，即可免费体验一个月的WHOOP。

sentences.en: Some people keep all their old gig tickets.
sentences.zh: 有些人保留着他们所有的旧演出门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music, it brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回音乐，唤回记忆，甚至连气味都能找回来。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则收集香水瓶、咖啡马克杯、海外纸币，或是80年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是一件极其个人化的事。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它诉说着我们是谁，但也诉说着我们从何而来。

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed with Sam Todd,
sentences.zh: 在全新播客《Sam Todd的迷人世界》中，

sentences.en: Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: Sam探索了那些构成我们一部分的记忆、执念和小珍宝。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 《Sam Todd的迷人世界》。

sentences.en: Stories want to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: 与Pandora合作打造的“想讲述的故事”。

sentences.en: Listen to the podcast now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在就在iHeart上收听这档播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to the Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《20多岁的心理学》，在这里我们探讨20多岁时面临的一些重大生活改变和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, you know the deal.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，你们都懂的。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听又一期节目，当然，我们要在这里剖析20多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about something that I think is on a lot of our radars in some capacity.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要聊一个我认为在某种程度上引起了我们很多人关注的话题。

sentences.en: Two of the biggest and I would say most noteworthy elements of our 20s are dating, figuring out that whole side of things,
sentences.zh: 20多岁时最大、我也认为最值得关注的两个方面是：约会——摸索这整块的事情，

sentences.en: and also our experiences with navigating our mental health.
sentences.zh: 以及我们应对心理健康问题的经历。

sentences.en: I think that those two things really define this period of life more significantly, more profoundly than anything else.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两件事比其他任何事情都更显著、更深刻地定义了人生的这个阶段。

sentences.en: They are at the center of a lot of the most life-changing experiences and moments during this chapter of our lives.
sentences.zh: 它们处于我们人生这个章节中许多最能改变人生的经历和时刻的核心。

sentences.en: I think a lot of the biggest revelations we have about who we are and who we want to become come from these two kind of facets.
sentences.zh: 我认为，关于我们是谁以及我们想成为什么样的人，我们所获得的大多数最大感悟都来自于这两个方面。

sentences.en: They come from who we're dating, how we're dating, our experiences with love and heartbreak and so many other facets and then also our experiences with coping
sentences.zh: 它们来自于我们和谁约会、我们如何约会、我们对爱与心碎的经历以及许多其他方面，同时也来自于我们如何应对的经历，

sentences.en: and coping with how our mind works and the ways that sometimes it betrays us.
sentences.zh: 以及应对我们的大脑如何运作、有时又是如何背叛我们的方式。

sentences.en: I think whilst a lot of us are out there looking for love, looking for connection, for inspiration, for long-term companionship, whatever it is that you're kind of searching for
sentences.zh: 我想，当我们在外面寻找爱、寻找连接、寻找灵感、寻找长期伴侣，无论你在约会生活中苦苦寻找的是什么时，

sentences.en: in your dating life, this is also the decade of quite a lot of mental struggle and I don't want to say suffering because I don't think that's the right word, but healing maybe
sentences.zh: 这也是一个伴随着相当多心理挣扎的十年，我不想用“痛苦”这个词，因为我觉得那不太合适，也许是治愈，

sentences.en: and also deep emotional work.
sentences.zh: 也是深刻的情感功课。

sentences.en: I think there's no denying the evidence, the research that 18 to 29-year-olds have the largest incidence rate of mental health symptoms, primarily anxiety and depression,
sentences.zh: 我认为无可否认的是，有证据和研究表明，18至29岁人群的心理健康症状发生率最高，主要是焦虑和抑郁，

sentences.en: than any other age group.
sentences.zh: 超过了任何其他年龄段。

sentences.en: We see it over and over again in studies all around the world.
sentences.zh: 我们在世界各地的研究中一次又一次地看到这一点。

sentences.en: Young people, 20-something-year-olds, they're really doing it tough when it comes to their mental health and whilst that is going on, we are also expected to make
sentences.zh: 年轻人，20出头的人，他们在心理健康方面确实过得很艰难，而在这一切发生的同时，我们也本该完成

sentences.en: that big transition into kind of what an adult should look like.
sentences.zh: 向所谓成年人样子的那种巨大转变。

sentences.en: We're meant to show people that we're growing up, that we're progressing, that they don't need to worry about us, you know, we're hitting the adult milestones.
sentences.zh: 我们本该向人们展示我们在长大，我们在进步，他们不用为我们担心，你知道的，我们在达成成年人的各个里程碑。

sentences.en: Part of that is dating, is having a relationship, is meeting people.
sentences.zh: 其中的一部分就是约会、谈恋爱、结识新朋友。

sentences.en: And what I don't think anybody is talking about is how mental health and dating really interact.
sentences.zh: 而我认为没有人真正在讨论的是，心理健康和约会之间究竟是如何相互影响的。

sentences.en: That relationship really needs to be explored in both directions because dating is honestly, it's such a vulnerable experience, it's so intimate.
sentences.zh: 这种关系确实需要从双向去探讨，因为约会老实说，真的是一种非常脆弱、非常亲密的体验。

sentences.en: You're basically sitting in front of a person and saying, please like me for who I am.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是坐在一个人面前说：“请喜欢本来的我吧。”

sentences.en: Maybe there's a future here.
sentences.zh: “也许我们之间会有未来。”

sentences.en: Yeah, please accept me.
sentences.zh: “是的，请接纳我。”

sentences.en: But also, you know, it's okay if you don't, like, I don't want to get too close to you.
sentences.zh: 但同时，你知道的，“如果你不接受也没关系，呃，我不想跟你走得太近。”

sentences.en: Like, it's this whole, I think, kind of mental maze.
sentences.zh: 就像，我觉得这完全是一种心理迷宫。

sentences.en: And our mental health is going to impact how we date, how we go about meeting new people, how those experiences will affect us.
sentences.zh: 我们的心理健康会影响我们如何约会、我们如何去结识新朋友，以及这些经历将如何影响我们。

sentences.en: And dating will also simultaneously
sentences.zh: 而约会也将同时

sentences.en: impact our mental health, the rejection, the heartbreak, the ups and downs.
sentences.zh: 影响我们的心理健康，那些拒绝、心碎、起起伏伏。

sentences.en: That really does something to our coping skills, to our mood, our confidence, our overall sense of emotional stability.
sentences.zh: 这确实会对我们的应对能力、情绪、自信心以及整体的情感稳定感产生影响。

sentences.en: And I think that's really important to recognize.
sentences.zh: 我认为认识到这一点真的很重要。

sentences.en: I also think part of the conversation around dating and mental health has to do with the partners of people with mental health struggles.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，关于约会和心理健康的讨论，有一部分与那些正经历心理健康挣扎的人的伴侣有关。

sentences.en: And what is it that they need to understand that maybe isn't communicated?
sentences.zh: 他们需要理解什么可能是没有被表达出来的呢？

sentences.en: You know, the things that people need from a relationship is, you know, it's going to differ.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们从一段关系中需要的东西，这会不尽相同。

sentences.en: It's going to differ based on things like preferences and attachment styles and past relationships, all of those things, but also based on where we are at mentally.
sentences.zh: 它会根据偏好、依恋类型、过去的恋爱经历等因素而有所不同，但也会根据我们当下的心理状态而改变。

sentences.en: If you're anxious, you might require, you know, more reassurance from your partner.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到焦虑，你可能需要，你知道的，来自伴侣更多的安抚。

sentences.en: If you're prone to depressive episodes, you might self-isolate.
sentences.zh: 如果你容易出现抑郁发作，你可能会自我隔离。

sentences.en: You might push people away and it doesn't mean that you don't care about them, that you don't want connection, that you are not deserving of connection.
sentences.zh: 你可能会把人推开，这并不意味着你在乎他们，不想要连接，不意味着你不配拥有连接。

sentences.en: I just think that it is something that is part of kind of like, not to sound cheesy, but our journey and it's part of how we find people who accept us for who we truly are.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这是，怎么说呢，虽然听起来可能有点俗气，但这是我们旅程的一部分，也是我们寻找真正接纳我们本色的人的一部分。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about it today.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天想聊聊这个。

sentences.en: I want to talk about every side of this connection, how everything interacts in this way and I think more importantly, how we can have both, how we can date successfully
sentences.zh: 我想讨论这种联系的每一面，所有这一切是如何以这种方式相互作用的，我想更重要的是，我们如何能兼得两者，如何能够成功约会

sentences.en: without letting it harm our most precious resource, which is our mental health.
sentences.zh: 而不让它伤害我们最宝贵的资源，也就是我们的心理健康。

sentences.en: How do we put up boundaries?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何设立界限？

sentences.en: How do we have hard conversations with the people we're seeing around what we need?
sentences.zh: 我们如何与正在交往的人就我们的需求进行艰难的对话？

sentences.en: How do we approach the things that maybe we want to hide from?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何面对那些我们可能想要逃避的事物？

sentences.en: How do we stop trauma bonding with people or letting people take advantage of us?
sentences.zh: 我们如何停止与人进行创伤式绑定，或者不再让别人占我们的便宜？

sentences.en: How do we kind of cope with dealing with simultaneously the crazy world of dating whilst also taking care of ourselves and taking care of our mental health?
sentences.zh: 我们如何在兼顾自我照顾和心理健康的同时，去应付约会这个疯狂的世界？

sentences.en: So we're going to talk about all of it, all the research, all the psychology, all the science and so much more.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要把这些全部聊透，所有的研究、所有的心理学、所有的科学以及更多内容。

sentences.en: So let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 让我们切入正题吧。

sentences.en: I want to start off by talking about how our mental health impacts how we date, how it changes the way that we date, our behavioural patterns, our attitudes towards dating.
sentences.zh: 我想从探讨我们的心理健康如何影响我们的约会方式开始，它如何改变我们的约会方式、我们的行为模式、我们对约会的态度。

sentences.en: I think mental health is not a one size fits all kind of concept.
sentences.zh: 我认为心理健康并不是一个“一刀切”的概念。

sentences.en: We can't just slap a label on everyone who could possibly have a diagnosis that falls into the DSM and call it mental health.
sentences.zh: 我们不能只是给每个可能符合精神疾病诊断手册（DSM）诊断标准的人贴上一个标签，然后就统称为心理健康。

sentences.en: I think different conditions are going to have a different impact when it comes to dating.
sentences.zh: 我认为不同的病症在涉及约会时会产生不同的影响。

sentences.en: And the main ones I really want to look at are really depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 而我真正想关注的主要还是抑郁症和焦虑症。

sentences.en: I think those have the highest prevalence, but there's also a lot to be said about the interactions between like ADHD and BPD and dating.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些是最普遍的，但关于多动症（ADHD）和边缘型人格障碍（BPD）与约会之间的相互作用，也有很多值得探讨的地方。

sentences.en: One of the biggest things that underpins all conditions, all mental health conditions is though, I think the experience of stigma that really persists to this day.
sentences.zh: 不过，支撑所有病症、所有心理健康状况的最核心因素之一，我认为是耻辱感的体验，这种耻辱感至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: We know that stigma shows up in the world and if it shows up in the world, it's going to show up in the people that we will meet.
sentences.zh: 我们知道耻辱感会出现在世界上，如果它出现在世界上，它就会出现在我们遇到的人身上。

sentences.en: Maybe the people we will date.
sentences.zh: 也许就是我们约会的人。

sentences.en: It will show up in the people we talk to.
sentences.zh: 它会出现在我们交谈的人身上。

sentences.en: As unfortunate and sad as that is and not everyone has the dialogue that perhaps we're having to understand that really it's not a reflection of who someone is
sentences.zh: 尽管这很不幸、很悲哀，而且并不是每个人都有我们现在正在进行的这种对话，去理解这其实并不反映一个人的本质，

sentences.en: that doesn't say anything about their worth.
sentences.zh: 这并不说明他们的价值。

sentences.en: So I think that's one of the primary things we have to navigate.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是我们必须应对的首要问题之一。

sentences.en: How do we have those open conversations around mental health with people that we're dating?
sentences.zh: 我们如何与正在约会的人就心理健康进行这些公开的对话？

sentences.en: When do we tell people?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候告诉别人？

sentences.en: Do we tell people?
sentences.zh: 我们要告诉别人吗？

sentences.en: What do we say?
sentences.zh: 我们要说些什么？

sentences.en: How do we respond when someone doesn't have a good response and they let us down?
sentences.zh: 当别人的反应不好并让我们失望时，我们该如何回应？

sentences.en: When they kind of reveal a part of themselves that like isn't willing to accept this.
sentences.zh: 当他们暴露出他们不愿意接受这一面的时候。

sentences.en: Especially if it's someone that you're getting serious with.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果那是你正打算认真对待的人。

sentences.en: I want to touch on that just a little bit later on.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会稍微触及这一点。

sentences.en: Firstly let's kind of break down what it is about conditions that may make dating different for different people who have some kind of experience with mental health.
sentences.zh: 首先，让我们剖析一下，心理健康状况究竟有哪些特点，可能会让有某种心理健康经历的不同人体验到不同的约会感受。

sentences.en: Depression is I was about to say depression is a good place to start but and I know that sounds so terrible but let's start there.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症是……我本想说抑郁症是一个很好的切入点，我知道这听起来太糟糕了，但我们就从这里开始吧。

sentences.en: Let's start there.
sentences.zh: 我们就从这里开始。

sentences.en: Depression I think I know makes it hard to do anything.
sentences.zh: 我认为抑郁症确实让做任何事情都变得很困难。

sentences.en: It is one of the primary underlying facts about this condition.
sentences.zh: 这是这种病情最基本的核心事实之一。

sentences.en: It makes it hard for you to be excited about anything in life.
sentences.zh: 它让你很难对生活中的任何事情感到兴奋。

sentences.en: You know let alone a random stranger you've met on a dating app.
sentences.zh: 更不用说你在约会软件上遇到的一个陌生人了。

sentences.en: Let alone the possibility of having to meet new people and tell them your favourite colour and let them get to know you.
sentences.zh: 更不用说去面对这种可能性：去认识新的人，告诉他们你最喜欢的颜色，让他们了解你。

sentences.en: I think depression also
sentences.zh: 我认为抑郁症还

sentences.en: causes us to self-isolate at times.
sentences.zh: 有时会导致我们自我隔离。

sentences.en: It means that we have less energy occasionally to put energy into the early stages of dating into going on dates into putting ourselves out there.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们偶尔会缺乏精力投入到约会的早期阶段，投入到约会中，去向外界展露自己。

sentences.en: It's really hard I think and important to acknowledge that it's going to be different if you're someone who has these episodes of just not feeling like the world is a great place
sentences.zh: 这真的很艰难，我认为必须承认这一点：如果你是一个经常觉得世界并不是个好地方的人，情况就会有所不同，

sentences.en: and maybe your response to that is to go silent is to self-isolate.
sentences.zh: 也许你对此的反应是陷入沉默，是自我隔离。

sentences.en: During those episodes I do feel like it's like everything stops and that can be hard for the people that we're dating to understand.
sentences.zh: 在那些阶段里，我确实感觉就像一切都停滞了，而这可能是我们约会对象很难理解的。

sentences.en: We might end up accidentally ghosting someone maybe icing them out and sometimes people don't understand that and that's not something that we can redeem ourselves from
sentences.zh: 我们最终可能会不小心“失联”（ghosting）某人，也许是将他们冷落，有时人们无法理解这一点，而这是我们无法挽回的，

sentences.en: or we let go of good connections because we honestly just don't have the mental bandwidth to maintain them.
sentences.zh: 或者我们放手了美好的连接，因为我们老实说实在没有足够的精神带宽去维持它们。

sentences.en: I think also depression has this awful habit of making us feel like we are not good people because we're not showing up in the way that people expect us to.
sentences.zh: 我也认为抑郁症有一个可怕的习惯，那就是让我们觉得自己不是好人，因为我们的表现没有达到别人的预期。

sentences.en: Let me talk about that a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 让我多聊聊这个。

sentences.en: I think like when we imagine dating especially in our 20s it is this like image of like fun and excitement and like ecstasy and like everything is new and amazing we're having
sentences.zh: 我觉得当我们想象约会时，尤其是在我们20多岁的时候，它呈现出的是一种充满乐趣、兴奋、狂喜的画面，就好像一切都是崭新的、惊奇的，我们正在经历

sentences.en: the best experiences and we're meeting people but sometimes you just don't feel like a fun person.
sentences.zh: 最棒的体验，我们在结识新朋友，但有时你就是觉得自己不是个有趣的人。

sentences.en: You just don't feel like you have the space to hold those experiences
sentences.zh: 你就是觉得自己没有空间去承载那些体验，

sentences.en: and that can make us feel like because we're not having the same experiences that everyone else is because we are struggling with something deeper that we are the problem.
sentences.zh: 这会让我们觉得，因为我们没有经历和别人一样的体验，因为我们在与更深层次的东西搏斗，所以我们自己就是问题所在。

sentences.en: We turn to a point of a lot of self-shame and one of the real big kind of
sentences.zh: 我们转向了充满自我羞耻的一点，而且其中一个真正重大的

sentences.en: negative self-talk points that I see we tell ourselves one of the things we often say is like
